description: Blacks in Cyber Village at DEF CON 30 showcases research on software supply chains, machine learning trustworthiness, digital financial privacy, and career growth systems.

talks.title: A Bridge Across the Digital Divide: Cryptocurrency, Central Bank Digital Currencies, & Economic Inclusion
talks.teaser: Stephanie Barnes examines cryptocurrency adoption in minority communities and the risks Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) pose without inclusive design.
talks.summary:
Cryptocurrency Adoption Across Minority Demographics

Demographic research highlights that Black investors represent one of the fastest-growing sectors in retail cryptocurrency adoption, seeking alternatives to traditional banking.

Evaluating the Promise and Risks of Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs)

Stephanie Barnes explores proposals for a US federal digital dollar, analyzing how government-backed digital currencies interact with existing mobile payment platforms.

Digital Surveillance and Account Freezes in Financial Applications

The author discusses the systemic vulnerabilities and account seizure risks observed in unregulated fintech payment apps (Cash App, PayPal, Venmo).

Ensuring Community Representation in Financial Architecture

The presentation emphasizes the critical necessity of including disenfranchised populations in the technical and policy design of future digital currency systems.

talks.title: Growth Systems for Cybersecurity Enthusiasts: Transitioning from Newbie to Expert
talks.teaser: Segun Olaniyan shares practical 'Growth Systems' for students and aspiring security practitioners to build industry credibility and accelerate their infosec careers.
talks.summary:
The Navigational Challenges of Entering Cybersecurity

Breaking into the cybersecurity industry often presents a daunting barrier for students and career switchers navigating conflicting advice and credential inflation.

Introducing Repeatable Professional Growth Systems

Segun Olaniyan outlines structured personal development frameworks designed to build verifiable technical competence, portfolio projects, and practical labs.

Establishing Industry Relevance as a Student

Olaniyan details actionable strategies for participating in capture-the-flag competitions, open-source tooling, and technical writing to establish industry credibility early.

Mentorship, Community Building, and Long-Term Success

The presentation highlights how active participation in local security groups and deliberate networking turn beginners into sought-after cybersecurity practitioners.

talks.title: The Last Log4j Talk You Ever Need: Minecraft Homelabs to Enterprise Supply Chains
talks.teaser: Ochuan Marshall breaks down Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228), demonstrating how to exploit JNDI lookups in a Minecraft homelab and secure software supply chains.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing the Log4Shell Vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228)

Log4Shell exposed systemic flaws in Java logging architectures, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to trigger arbitrary JNDI lookups over LDAP.

Building a Local Minecraft Homelab with Vagrant

Ochuan Marshall demonstrates setting up an isolated virtual test environment with older Java and Minecraft server builds to observe JNDI lookups in real time.

Weaponizing JNDI Lookup Injections via Chat Messages

The speaker illustrates how injecting a simple `${jndi:ldap://...}` payload into in-game chat or web headers executes remote code with minimal friction.

Supply Chain Hardening and Application Security Lessons

The presentation provides decision-makers and engineers with actionable strategies for auditing third-party Java dependencies and enforcing secure logging configurations.

talks.title: Neurodiversity in Cybersecurity: Find Your Competitive Advantage
talks.teaser: Kassandra Pierre and Nathan Chung explore how neurodiverse cognitive traits (ADHD, autism) provide distinct analytical advantages in cybersecurity operations.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, phishing techniques, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses in organizations.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: DEI in Cybersecurity: Breaking Through Implicit Barriers & Vaulting Gatekeepers
talks.teaser: Damian Grant shares personal experiences and actionable strategies for overcoming systemic barriers and implicit bias to thrive in technical cybersecurity roles.
talks.summary:
The Paradox of the Cybersecurity Skills Shortage

While the cybersecurity industry continuously reports millions of unfilled jobs, talented minority professionals encounter significant barriers to entry and upward mobility.

Navigating Implicit Bias and Institutional Gatekeeping

Damian Grant explores the structural challenges faced by Black professionals in STEM, analyzing hiring biases, gatekeeping credentials, and workplace culture friction.

Actionable Strategies for Technical Mastery and Advancement

Grant outlines concrete approaches for building hands-on technical skillsets, cultivating sponsorship, and commanding professional value in high-demand specialties.

Fostering Sustainable Inclusion Across the Industry

The presentation challenges organizations to move beyond performative diversity initiatives by reforming hiring pipelines and creating equitable advancement pathways.

talks.title: State of the Model: Security, Privacy, & Trustworthiness in High-Stakes Machine Learning
talks.teaser: Dr. Birhanu Eshete evaluates the trustworthiness of machine learning models in healthcare, autonomous driving, and finance, analyzing adversarial attacks and fairness pitfalls.
talks.summary:
The High-Stakes Proliferation of Machine Learning

Machine learning models are rapidly deployed in critical decision-making systems—including autonomous vehicles, clinical healthcare diagnostics, and algorithmic credit scoring.

Analyzing Security and Privacy Pitfalls in Modern ML

Dr. Birhanu Eshete categorizes core threat vectors—such as adversarial example perturbation, training data poisoning, and model inversion attacks.

Evaluating Transparency, Explainability, and Algorithmic Fairness

The author explores how uncurated training data perpetuates demographic biases and examines technical metrics for verifying algorithmic fairness and model transparency.

Roadmap for Trustworthy and Resilient AI Deployments

The presentation outlines defense-in-depth frameworks, differential privacy mechanisms, and robust verification protocols for deploying dependable AI systems.

talks.title: The Man in the Middle: Covert Communication, Resistance, & Overcoming Surveillance
talks.teaser: EFF Director of Engineering Alexis Hancock draws parallels between historical resistance against slavery surveillance and modern anti-censorship tools.
talks.summary:
Historical Precedents of Pervasive Surveillance and Control

During the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade, enslavers enforced extreme surveillance, language suppression, and physical separation to prevent organizing and resistance.

Covert Channels, Steganography, and Coded Communication

Alexis Hancock examines how enslaved Africans developed resilient covert communication channels—using music, spirituals, visual patterns, and linguistic steganography.

Connecting Historical Resistance to Modern Anti-Surveillance Tooling

Hancock draws direct parallels between historical resistance systems and modern privacy technologies—such as end-to-end encrypted messaging, Tor, and mesh networks.

Reclaiming Community Connection Against Modern Authoritarianism

The presentation emphasizes the enduring imperative of building decentralized, open-source communications infrastructure to resist state and corporate surveillance.
